title: Tea Emoji 🍵 Meaning: Matcha, Calm and Spilling the Tea
description: 🍵 shows a handleless cup of green tea. It means tea, matcha and calm moments, and it is the emoji for “spill the tea” gossip. See examples and tips.
summary: The 🍵 teacup without handle emoji shows Japanese-style green tea. It means tea, matcha, relaxation and self-care. In slang it represents “tea,” meaning gossip or the truth about a situation. It is used to ask for, promise or react to juicy information.
meaning: The cup in this emoji is a yunomi, the handleless vessel used for everyday green tea in Japan, and the liquid is clearly green. That makes 🍵 the most literal tea emoji available. People use it for matcha lattes, sencha, herbal blends, sushi restaurants and tea ceremonies. Since the worldwide matcha boom, it has also become a wellness symbol, appearing in morning-routine videos and café photos with a whisk and a pale green drink.

Mood is the second meaning. Tea implies slowing down, so 🍵 marks quiet evenings, sick days, rainy afternoons and deliberate calm. Someone who replies to chaos with a single 🍵 may be saying they are unbothered. It is the visual shorthand for “I'm staying in tonight” and for small acts of looking after yourself. Paired with a book, a blanket or a candle, it sets a whole scene.

Then comes gossip. “Tea” as slang for inside information spread from Black drag communities into mainstream internet speech, giving us “spill the tea,” “that's the tea” and “piping hot tea.” 🍵 is the usual emoji for it, along with the coffee cup. “The 🍵 is scalding” means the gossip is excellent. “No 🍵, no shade” prefaces an honest remark the speaker claims is not an attack.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends open with “I have 🍵” to announce news worth a phone call. The reply “spill” follows instantly. In calmer use it reports what someone is drinking or signals winding down for the night. It also offers gentle care, as in telling a sick friend to rest and drink something warm.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Two worlds share it. Drama and commentary channels use 🍵 for exposés and storytimes. Lifestyle creators use it for matcha recipes, tea hauls and soft, green-toned aesthetics. The surrounding content makes the meaning obvious, and occasionally a creator plays on both by spilling gossip while whisking matcha.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: In Japan, China and elsewhere in East Asia the emoji is ordinary and literal, simply meaning tea. British users sometimes prefer ☕ for their milky black tea, since the green drink does not match. In English-speaking internet culture generally, the gossip sense is as common as the beverage.

examples.text: Call me. I have 🍵 and it's HOT
examples.meaning: The sender has exciting gossip to share.
A literal drink, part of a wellness routine.

examples.text: Staying in tonight. Tea, blanket, done 🍵
That's the 🍵, do with it what you will
examples.meaning: Concluding a piece of gossip or a blunt truth.

examples.text: Feel better soon, lots of 🍵 and rest
No 🍵 no shade but that haircut was a choice
examples.meaning: Offering criticism while claiming it is not meant unkindly.

combos.meaning: Ready for gossip, or reacting to it.
The Kermit “none of my business” meme, sipping after a pointed remark.
Green tea, matcha or a calm, natural mood.
A quiet moment with tea and a book.

confusedWith.difference: ☕ is a generic steaming cup on a saucer, read by most people as coffee. Both can mean gossip, but 🍵 is the true tea emoji and the better match for matcha and calm.
🧋 is iced milk tea with tapioca pearls and a wide straw. It signals boba runs and hanging out, not serenity or gossip.
🧉 shows yerba mate in a gourd with a metal straw, a South American drink. It is used for mate culture in Argentina, Uruguay and neighboring countries.

avoid: Don't announce “🍵” about someone's private struggles; sharing sensitive information as entertainment can do real harm.
Avoid “no tea, no shade” as cover for a harsh insult, since readers will see through it.
design: A small cup without a handle, filled with green tea, appears on all major platforms. The cup is often shown in a neutral ceramic tone, sometimes with a pattern or a darker base, and some designs add steam or a saucer-like coaster. The green liquid is the constant feature and the reason it reads as tea, not coffee.

faqs.a: It means “tea,” which is gossip, secrets or the real story. To spill the tea is to reveal it. The expression originated in Black drag culture and spread widely through social media and reality television.

faqs.q: What does 🍵 mean from a girl or guy?
faqs.a: Either they have gossip, they want yours, or they are literally having tea and relaxing. A message like “🍵?” after you mention drama is a request for details. It is not a romantic signal by itself.

It depicts Japanese green tea, and people use it for matcha all the time, although whisked matcha is traditionally served in a wider bowl. There is no separate matcha emoji, so this one is the accepted stand-in.

The first is green tea in a handleless cup, tied to calm, wellness and gossip. The second is a general hot drink, usually taken as coffee, tied to mornings and meetups. Both are used for “tea” in the gossip sense.

faqs.q: When was the tea emoji added?
faqs.a: It was included in the original standardized emoji set of 2010, reflecting the emoji keyboard's Japanese origins, where green tea is an everyday drink.
